events.title: Henry Hudson Discovers Delaware Bay
events.description: While searching for a passage to Asia aboard the Halve Maen for the Dutch East India Company, English explorer Henry Hudson sighted the broad inlet now known as Delaware Bay.
events.significance: The discovery fed into Hudson's famous voyage up the river that now bears his name. It also helped underpin Dutch claims in North America.

events.title: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe Is Born
events.description: Goethe was born in Frankfurt into a prosperous family and was educated at home. He grew up to write Faust and The Sorrows of Young Werther.
events.significance: He is regarded as one of the giants of world literature and shaped German culture, poetry, and drama for generations.

events.title: Herschel Discovers Saturn's Moon Enceladus
events.description: Using a large telescope he built himself, astronomer William Herschel spotted a new moon orbiting Saturn.
events.significance: Enceladus is now known to have geysers venting from a hidden subsurface ocean. That makes it one of the most promising places to look for life beyond Earth.

events.title: 'I Have a Dream' at the March on Washington
events.description: About 250,000 people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial for the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom. There Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech.
events.significance: The speech became a defining moment of the American civil rights movement. It helped build momentum for the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

events.title: New Orleans Ordered to Evacuate Ahead of Hurricane Katrina
events.description: As Hurricane Katrina grew into a catastrophic storm in the Gulf of Mexico, Mayor Ray Nagin issued the first mandatory evacuation order in the city's history.
events.significance: Katrina flooded most of New Orleans and killed more than 1,000 people. The disaster exposed deep flaws in US emergency preparedness and prompted major reforms.
